newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aluminium, zinc prices set to rise - Mocatta.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aluminium, zinc prices set to rise - Mocatta.

text.p: Aluminium was expected to continue its steady upward price progression from a two and a half year low, Mocatta Base Metals, a division of Standard Chartered Bank Australia Ltd, said in its monthly report.
Aluminium had a constructive month in October after its slump, Mocatta said.
The market continued to see good trade support at the lower levels and while the economic picture did not point to extreme growth, it remained positive, it said.
September's decline in aluminium prices continued into October but a bounce was epitomised by a US$45.00 a tonne surge on October 23 from $1,366.00 a tonne.
Once resistance was broken at the psychological $1,400 barrier, positive sentiment maintained prices above this crucial level to month's end, Mocatta said.
Copper continued to be unable to break its broad established range during October but could breach its current $1,850-$2,050 a tonne range if stocks continued to decline, it said.
Failure to break through the October high of $2,047 toward the end of the month brought a selloff to $1,900 over three days, it said.
But Mocatta said on balance it was less inclined to follow bullish views. It advocated scale up hedge selling of copper into any strength.
Lead's bounce at month's end was steady but unconvincing with technical indicators still pointing to a continuing downward trend, it said.
A price fall in the latter part of the month to a nine-month low at $710 a tonne led to a bounce as trade buyers provided a foothold and profit-takers added momentum to the bounce, it said.
"These two factors offered a sound base for a controlled retracement to the end of the month up to the resistence level around $760," it said.
From a technical view, lead was oversold at the $715 support level, Mocatta said.
Consumer interest as the price weakened indicated a short-term move by lead back to $750-$760, but it would struggle to move much higher, Mocatta said.
Mocatta saw $600 rather than $900 as lead's likely objective for 1997.
A change in sentiment seemed set to take the zinc market higher, Mocatta said.
Despite the possibility of a correction, with the price having broken $1,060 a tonne, the next objective of $1,120 may be achieved as early as November, it said.
Longer-term, a target of $1,200-$1,250 beckoned for 1997, it said.
Zinc's outlook was promising with continued gradual but consistent LME stock drawdowns, Mocatta said.
